venues.Sno-Isle Libraries: The public library system for Snohomish and Island counties, with branches in nearly every town around Everett. Almost everything is free: storytimes, classes, author talks and book groups.
venues.Schack Art Center: A downtown Everett arts center with free galleries and a working glass hot shop you can watch from the floor. Most of what is listed here are classes, so check the age and sign-up details on the Schack’s page. Lots of events for kids and adults.
venues.Funko Field: The ballpark at Everett Memorial Stadium on Broadway, home of the AquaSox. A local favorite. It is a small park where every seat is close to the field.
venues.Angel of the Winds Arena: Everett’s downtown arena on Hewitt Avenue, home ice of the Silvertips and the stop for big touring concerts and family shows. Downtown’s bars and restaurants are a short walk away, so it is easy to make a night of it. Largest event space in Everett.
venues.Scuttlebutt Brewing: One of Everett’s hometown breweries, pouring since 1996, with a family restaurant on the waterfront and a taproom at the brewery. Expect trivia, live music and beer releases.
venues.Port of Everett: The waterfront: the marina, Waterfront Place and Boxcar Park. Summer brings outdoor concerts and the Sunday farmers market, and the holidays bring lights along the docks. And... a lot of new sweet restaurants. It is the biggest active new bar/restaurant area in Everett.
venues.Everett Public Library: The city’s own library, with the main branch downtown on Hoyt Avenue and the Evergreen Branch in south Everett. Events are free and lean toward local history, authors and kids.
venues.City of Snohomish: Events put on by the City of Snohomish, about fifteen minutes east of Everett: parades, markets and community gatherings.
venues.APEX Everett: The APEX Art and Culture Center fills the old Masonic temple on Everett Avenue downtown, with Kings Hall for concerts and several smaller rooms under one roof.
venues.Lucky Dime: A small bar on Hewitt Avenue in downtown Everett with local and touring bands on its stage. It is 21 and over.
venues.City of Mill Creek: Community events from the City of Mill Creek, south of Everett, many of them around Mill Creek Town Center.
venues.El Sid: A bar and music room inside the APEX building downtown, with blues nights, local bands and DJs. It is 21 and over.
venues.Historic Downtown Snohomish: First Street in Snohomish: antique shops, restaurants and the riverfront, with wine walks, car shows and holiday events through the year.
venues.City of Everett: Events the City of Everett puts on itself: parades, park concerts, the Fourth of July and seasonal festivals. Most are free.
venues.Tulalip Resort Casino: The casino resort north of Everett, just off I-5. Shows are in the Orca Ballroom, and most are 21 and over.
venues.City of Marysville: Community events from the City of Marysville, just north of Everett across the river: the Strawberry Festival season, park concerts and holiday lights.
venues.Village Theatre: Professional musical theatre at the Everett Performing Arts Center on Wetmore Avenue downtown. Each show plays for several weeks, with evening and matinee performances.
venues.Historic Everett Theatre: Everett’s oldest theatre, opened in 1901 on Colby Avenue downtown. It hosts tribute bands, comedy, classic films and community shows.
venues.Edmonds Center for the Arts: A 700-seat hall in a restored school auditorium in Edmonds, about half an hour south of Everett, with touring music, dance and speakers.
venues.City of Mukilteo: Community events from the City of Mukilteo, by the ferry and the lighthouse southwest of Everett.

teams.silvertips: Everett’s Western Hockey League team, at Angel of the Winds Arena since 2003. The players are 16 to 20 years old and many go on to the NHL; games are loud, fast and good for families.
teams.aquasox: The Seattle Mariners’ High-A affiliate, playing at Funko Field from April into September. Tickets are cheap, the park is small, and tomorrow’s Mariners come through here first.
teams.trojans: Everett Community College’s teams, playing other Northwest community colleges. Home games are on campus in north Everett.
teams.wolfpack: Everett’s indoor football team, playing at Angel of the Winds Arena since 2024. The season runs in spring and summer.
